import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.62

by A. I. Sozutov

Construct a group with no subgroup of index $2$ that is generated by a
conjugacy class $X$ of involutions, such that the product of any two elements
of $X$ has finite odd order. The parenthetical version additionally asks that
the group be periodic.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.62»

/--
Does there exist a group $G$ with no subgroup of index $2$, generated by a
conjugacy class $X$ of an involution, such that the product of every two
elements of $X$ has finite odd order?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (x : G) (X : Set G),
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      X = conjugatesOf x ∧
      Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ a ∈ X, ∀ b ∈ X, Odd (orderOf (a * b)) := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a periodic group $G$ with no subgroup of index $2$, generated
by a conjugacy class $X$ of an involution, such that the product of every two
elements of $X$ has finite odd order?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62».variants.periodic : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (x : G) (X : Set G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      X = conjugatesOf x ∧
      Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ a ∈ X, ∀ b ∈ X, Odd (orderOf (a * b)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.62»
modeling_decisions: Represented the conjugacy class X explicitly by existentially quantifying X and requiring `X = conjugatesOf x`, where the witnessed representative satisfies `orderOf x = 2`.
Expressed generation by X as `Subgroup.closure X = ⊤`.
Expressed absence of index-two subgroups as `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2`.
Used `Odd (orderOf (a * b))`; since Mathlib's `orderOf` is zero for an element of infinite order, oddness also enforces finiteness.
Formalized the optional periodic strengthening by adding `Monoid.IsTorsion G` and leaving every other condition unchanged.

by A. I. Sozutov

Does there exist a group $G$ with no subgroup of index $2$ and an involution $x \in G$ whose
conjugacy class $X$ generates $G$, such that $yz$ has finite odd order for every $y,z \in X$?

      X = {y | ∃ g : G, y = g * x * g⁻¹} ∧

      Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ y ∈ X, ∀ z ∈ X, Odd (orderOf (y * z)) := by
  sorry

whose conjugacy class $X$ generates $G$, such that $yz$ has odd order for every $y,z \in X$?

      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      X = {y | ∃ g : G, y = g * x * g⁻¹} ∧
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ y ∈ X, ∀ z ∈ X, Odd (orderOf (y * z)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.62»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.62

by A. I. Sozutov

Construct an example of a (periodic) group without subgroups of index 2 which is
generated by a conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the
product of any two involutions from $X$ is odd.

The problem is formalized as the existence question: does such a group exist?
The base statement omits the parenthetical "periodic"; the variant adds it as
the extra hypothesis that every element of the group has finite order.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.62»

/--
Does there exist a group $G$ without subgroups of index 2 which is generated by a
conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product of any two
involutions from $X$ is odd?

Here $X$ is a conjugacy class of $G$ all of whose elements have order exactly 2,
$G$ is the subgroup generated by $X$, and for all $x, y \in X$ the element $xy$
has odd order (in particular finite order).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (X : ConjClasses G),
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ X.carrier, orderOf x = 2) ∧
      Subgroup.closure X.carrier = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ x ∈ X.carrier, ∀ y ∈ X.carrier, Odd (orderOf (x * y)) := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a periodic group $G$ without subgroups of index 2 which is
generated by a conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the
product of any two involutions from $X$ is odd?

This is the stronger form indicated by the parenthetical "(periodic)": every
element of $G$ is required to have finite order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62».variants.periodic : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (X : ConjClasses G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ X.carrier, orderOf x = 2) ∧
      Subgroup.closure X.carrier = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ x ∈ X.carrier, ∀ y ∈ X.carrier, Odd (orderOf (x * y)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.62»

/-!
# Conjecture 10.62

by A. I. Sozutov

Construct an example of a (periodic) group without subgroups of index $2$ which is
generated by a conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product
of any two involutions from $X$ is odd.

The problem is stated as a construction; it is formalised as the question of whether
such a group exists. The parenthetical "(periodic)" is an optional stronger
requirement and is stated as a separate variant. No finite (or locally finite) group
has these properties, by Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem, so any example must be infinite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.62»

/--
Does there exist a group $G$ without subgroups of index $2$ which is generated by a
conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product of any two
involutions from $X$ is odd?

Here $X$ is the conjugacy class of an involution $x$ (an element of order $2$), so $G$
is generated by $X$ means $\langle X \rangle = G$. Since `orderOf` is `0` for an element
of infinite order, `Odd (orderOf (y * z))` says that $yz$ has finite odd order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (x : G),
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      Subgroup.closure (conjugatesOf x) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ z ∈ conjugatesOf x, Odd (orderOf (y * z)) := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a periodic group $G$ (every element of $G$ has finite order) without
subgroups of index $2$ which is generated by a conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such
that the order of the product of any two involutions from $X$ is odd?

This is the stronger form given by the parenthetical "(periodic)" in the statement.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62».variants.periodic : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (x : G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      Subgroup.closure (conjugatesOf x) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ z ∈ conjugatesOf x, Odd (orderOf (y * z)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.62»

modeling_decisions: 'Construct an example of ...' is read as the existence question 'Does there exist ...?' and stated in the repository's `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ...` style, following the decomposition table.
Involution is formalized as `orderOf x = 2` (this excludes x = 1); the conjugacy class X is `conjugatesOf x` = {b | IsConj x b}, which in a group is {g * x * g⁻¹}.
'Generated by X' is `Subgroup.closure (conjugatesOf x) = ⊤`.
'No subgroups of index 2' is `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2`; `Subgroup.index` returns 0 for infinite index, so this is exactly the intended condition.
